Open an app in a new tab to run R in your browser. The first launch downloads R and the
required packages. The [Shiny walkthrough](shiny.html) explains the code behind
the examples.

```{r gallery, echo=FALSE}
library(htmltools)

card <- function(app, title, description) {
  tags$div(
    class = "col",
    tags$a(
      class = "card h-100 text-decoration-none text-body",
      href = paste0("../live/", app, "/index.html"),
      target = "_blank",
      rel = "noopener",
      tags$img(
        class = "card-img-top",
        src = paste0("../shiny-gallery/", app, ".webp"),
        alt = ""
      ),
      tags$div(
        class = "card-body",
        tags$h2(class = "h5 mt-0 mb-2", title),
        tags$p(class = "mb-0", description)
      )
    )
  )
}

tags$div(
  class = "shiny-gallery row row-cols-1 row-cols-md-2 g-3",
  card(
    "basic",
    "Old Faithful",
    "Choose an eruption duration to see how long visitors waited for the next eruption."
  ),
  card(
    "proxy",
    "Proxy playground",
    "Compare cities, extend a passenger forecast, or rearrange an item chart using Shiny proxies."
  ),
  card(
    "events",
    "Equalizer",
    "Drag a frequency band and compare its live gain with the final value on release."
  ),
  card(
    "linked",
    "Linked charts",
    "Hover or click a species in the dotplot to see its flowers in the same color."
  ),
  card(
    "stock",
    "Stock prices",
    "Zoom from weekly SPY closes to daily prices for the selected dates."
  ),
  card(
    "theme",
    "Solar cycles",
    "Switch the observatory from daylight to night to see the chart inherit the app’s theme."
  )
)
```
